spec.name: Ventus Ambulare
spec.description: A Theo Jansen style wind-walking beach creature: pale PVC tube skeleton with jointed walking legs, a ribbed spine, a tall fabric wing sail and wind-organ pipes, resting on tidal sand.
spec.layout: A large kinetic beach animal seen in profile from +Z: a horizontal backbone of pale straw PVC tube runs along z at about 2.9 m high, rising at the bow into a neck and a head cluster of nose tubes with two dark lens eyes; wind-organ pipes hang under the bow. Mid-spine a tall mast carries a cream triangular wing sail to 6 m with a coral pennant on top. Behind, the backbone tapers into a two-joint tail with thin membrane fins and more organ pipes. Three jointed walking legs stand on each side (front z=2.0, mid z=0.3, rear z=-1.4): each is a triangle yoke from the spine out to a hip, then thigh, shin and a flat fin foot resting on y=0; elbow and knee joints wear dark knuckle discs and thin tie-rod lines. Every part reads as Theo Jansen construction: faceted PVC tube sweeps in pale straw and bone white, dark ink joints, rusted brackets, cream sail cloth, nothing smooth or organic.

parts.builds: The backbone, neck, head and bow organs. Sweep one continuous PVC backbone tube along spine0-spine1-spine2, radius about 0.14 tapering to 0.10, in palette tube with a thin tubeLight ring band at each spine joint. From spine0 sprout the neck chain up to head and sweep it, 0.10 tapering to 0.07, same tube. The head is a cluster, not a solid: at the head joint fan five short nose tubes (rods of tube and tubeLight, 0.05 radius, different lengths 0.25-0.45, slightly fanned), and seat two lens eyes as flat dark lens discs with pale lensRim rings on short stalks either side of the head, facing +Z. Add a brow tube arcing over the eyes in tubeDark. Ribs: 6 arc ribs (swept arcs, 0.035 radius, tubeLight) bowing out from the backbone to x=±0.45 at spread z stations between z=1.9 and z=-1.8, each rib capped with a small rust bracket cube at its base on the spine. Under the bow (z 1.9 to 2.6) hang 7 wind-organ pipes: vertical frustum tubes of tube and tubeDark, lengths 0.5-1.0 staggered, each with a rust collar ring at its mouth, hanging from a short header tube of tubeDark. All joints and brackets are small knuckle discs and rust cubes seated on the tube surface.
parts.attaches: Neck sprouts from spine0 near the bowNeck mount; sail mast steps onto the backbone tube at mastBase; tail sweeps onward from tailRoot; rib tips stay clear of the leg yoke boxes (x <= 0.55).

parts.builds: The mast, wing sail and rigging. A tapered mast (sweep along a short chain from mount mastBase to [0, 5.9, 1.05], radius 0.09 to 0.04, tube) with a lathe cap finial at the top in tubeLight and a coral pennant blade (extrude, pennant with ink stripe part) at the masthead. A boom of tube (0.06 radius) runs from mastBase back to z=-0.2, and a horizontal wing spar of tubeLight juts forward to z=1.8. The sail cloth is a membrane skinned between mast line and boom, palette sail, with a sailEdge trim band swept along its trailing edge and thin rope lines (0.012, rope) running diagonally from boom ends up to the mast at three heights, tied with small knuckle knots. Add a small wind-vane arrow of rust at mid-mast pointing into the wind (+Z). The sail reads as taut flat cloth with visible edge trim, held by rigid-looking tube spar edges.
parts.attaches: Mast base sits exactly on mount mastBase on the backbone tube of keel; boom end and spars stay above the stern box and clear of the keel head.

parts.builds: The tail and rear organs. Sweep the tail tube from mount tailRoot along tail1-tail2, radius 0.09 tapering to 0.03, in tube with a tubeDark band at tail1. Two thin vertical membrane fins (sail cloth, sailEdge edges) rise from the tail at z=-2.6 and z=-3.4 like shark fins, plus one small horizontal stabiliser membrane at tail2. A rear wind organ: 5 short pipes of tubeDark and rust of staggered length 0.3-0.6 fan upward and outward from a header tube clamped under the tail at z=-2.3, each with a rust collar. Tie the fin roots with rope wraps (thin rope sweeps) and add a knuckle disc at the tail2 joint.
parts.attaches: Tail sweep starts exactly at mount tailRoot, continuing the keel backbone tube so the two read as one continuous pipe.

parts.builds: All three left-side (+X) walking legs. For each leg (hipL/kneeL/footL at z 2.0, 0.3, -1.4): a yoke frame of tube (0.05 radius rods) runs as a triangle from the spine surface at y=2.85 out to mount yokeL/yoke points (front and rear yokes branch from the mid yoke line at [1.35, 2.75, 0.3]), ending in a hip knuckle disc (knuckle, 0.09 radius, with a rust bolt stud). The leg proper: thigh sweep hip to knee (0.075 radius, tube), shin sweep knee to foot (0.06, tubeLight), and a knee knuckle disc (knuckle with tubeLight rim). The foot is a flat fin paddle: an extruded trapezoid blade, 0.5 long along z, 0.05 thick, palette tubeDark with a tubeLight top edge, lying flat with its lowest face touching y=0. Each leg carries a crank drive: a rust crank disc (0.14 radius, 6-spoke) on a short axle at the hip, with a thin tie rod (0.012, rope) running from the crank down to the shin midpoint, plus one rust bracket where the yoke meets the spine. Legs are identical modules placed at the three z stations, front foot angled slightly forward.
parts.attaches: Yoke frames bolt to the keel backbone spine surface at x=0.5 near the spine joints; the mid yoke apex sits exactly at mount yokeL; every foot fin rests flat on y=0.

parts.builds: All three right-side (-X) walking legs, the exact mirror of legsL. For each leg (hipR/kneeR/footR at z 2.0, 0.3, -1.4): a yoke frame of tube (0.05 radius rods) runs as a triangle from the spine surface at y=2.85 out to mount yokeR (front and rear yokes branch from the mid yoke line at [-1.35, 2.75, 0.3]), ending in a hip knuckle disc (knuckle, 0.09 radius, with a rust bolt stud). The leg proper: thigh sweep hip to knee (0.075 radius, tube), shin sweep knee to foot (0.06, tubeLight), and a knee knuckle disc (knuckle with tubeLight rim). The foot is a flat fin paddle: an extruded trapezoid blade, 0.5 long along z, 0.05 thick, palette tubeDark with a tubeLight top edge, lying flat with its lowest face touching y=0. Each leg carries a rust crank disc (0.14 radius, 6-spoke) on a short hip axle with a rope tie rod down to the shin midpoint, plus one rust bracket where the yoke meets the spine. Mirror the left side exactly so the pair reads as one engineered machine.
parts.attaches: Yoke frames bolt to the keel backbone spine surface at x=-0.5 near the spine joints; the mid yoke apex sits exactly at mount yokeR; every foot fin rests flat on y=0.

I need to write a spec JSON for a "wind-walking beach creature of tubes" in Theo Jansen Strandbeest style. Team of builders, 3-6 parts, shared spec with mounts, joints, palette, boxes, budgets.

Theo Jansen Strandbeest: PVC yellow piping (light warm yellow/tan), sails/wings from fabric, multiple walking legs with triangle linkage joints, wind sail. Let me design.

Concept: a large wind-walking beach creature ~6m long, 4.5m tall, 3.5m wide. Skeleton: central spine tube running along z, with a wind organ, sail mast, leg frames on both sides, walking legs with jointed knee joints.

Parts (5):
1. spine/hull: central backbone tube, ribs, head/bow, neck. Contains spine joints.
2. sail rig: mast, fabric sail panels, tail fins, wind vane.
3. leg frames: shoulder/yoke structures connecting spine to legs, plus hips.
4. walking legs: the many PVC tube legs with joints (left side + right side? maybe split left and right legs to balance work). Let's do 6 parts: spine+head, sail, tail, legsL, legsR, leg frame? Budgets add ≤900.

Plan parts:
- "keel" (spine & head): backbone tube along z, neck, head with nose tube cluster, ribs, wind organ pipes at front. Budget 200.
- "sail" (mast & wings): mast, sails, pennants. Budget 150.
- "stern" (tail & pump): tail tube frame, fins, wind organ pipes. Budget 140.
- "legsL": left-side walking legs (3 legs), each a leg made of PVC tubes with joints. Budget 180.
- "legsR": mirror. Budget 180.
Total ~850.

Joints: root spine at front? Chain of spine joints: spine0 (root), spine1, spine2... Tail joints tail1..tail3. Head/neck joints. Leg joints: hipL1..3, kneeL..., footL... Many joints. Skeleton should be reasonable — Strandbeests have many leg joints. Maybe legs as rigid tubes with hinge joints at hips and knees for animation.
